measured_rules: Descriptor lookup precedes version and output validation; invalid and closed descriptors return EBADF 9.
Versions 0, 1, 4 and -1 return EINVAL 22 after successful descriptor lookup.
Read-only, write-only and read-write descriptors support metadata lookup.
An inherited descriptor remains usable after dropping to uid/gid 1234, even when the file has no access permission bits.
Closing and reopening the same descriptor observes the newly opened file.
A copy crossing an inaccessible page writes the accessible prefix then returns EFAULT.
All reserved fields and structure padding are zero.
The o32 version-2 size field saturates at INT32_MAX; n32 version 2 and both version-3 interfaces preserve the tested 64-bit size.
The v1 sentinel and tested n32 saved register survive direct and indirect calls.
native_differences: Device/inode identity, directory size, timestamps and allocation reflect the native filesystem, checked using an independent native fstat observer.
Filesystem name is unknown; project ID is zero because project accounting is not implemented.
unqualified: Sockets, anonymous pipes and other descriptor types beyond regular files, directory, FIFO and /dev/null
Concurrent close/reuse of descriptors and foreign signal interruption
Other historical version selectors beyond the tested rejected values
Inode, block-count, timestamp or device values beyond encoded widths
IRIX project accounting and XFS attributes
General IRIX application or desktop compatibility
fixture_limits: The reference changes primary uid/gid without clearing supplementary groups; the native runner clears them. Final fixtures avoid supplementary-group-dependent access checks. The initial mode-0751 directory setup diverged before fxstat; final directory mode is 0755 on both.
